stakeholders.name: Julian Maro
stakeholders.title: CIO
stakeholders.stance_summary: Supports expansion if downtime risk and reporting are addressed. "Directionally, the proof passed" but requires two remediation items before commercial approval. Wants decision by late May and emphasizes that the strategic recommendation should be "proceed, but not rush." Needs proof scorecard, incident ownership clarity, and consequence mapping if export slips. Cautions against "victory lap" framing—wants a close plan focused on making "the first rollout to be boring." Perceives competitor as simpler but notes Meridian has not validated their segmentation depth.

stakeholders.name: Clara Esteves
stakeholders.title: Director of Plant Systems
stakeholders.stance_summary: Strong champion for factory rollout. "The factory teams responded well to the shorter runbook. The shift supervisors liked the owner mapping." Emphasizes that under-supporting rollout is more expensive than bounded enablement and argues that capped services cannot remove support needed for success. Demands conditional approval only with documented retest dates and owner assignment: "I can support a conditional approval if the retest has a date and owner. Without that, I look like I am hand-waving." Insists on distinction between ready now, remediation, and roadmap items to maintain internal credibility. Advocates for proof-of-concept structure with executive scorecard and layered technical appendices.

stakeholders.name: Niko Hart
stakeholders.title: Network Operations Manager
stakeholders.stance_summary: Concerned about operational complexity and visibility gaps during failover. "I need the export retest and the incident owner map. If those pass, I will support expansion." Requires simplified incident view reliable during failover and clear ownership mapping across factory IT, central network, security, and vendor. Notes that "reporting export is not fatal, but pretending it did not happen would damage trust." Wants alert severity mapping so plant staff know "what can wait until morning." Acknowledges competitor is attractive to operations when "operations is tired" but validates vendor's segmentation approach. Requests incident ownership map maintenance and policy drift monitoring as ongoing commitments.

stakeholders.name: Lena Frost
stakeholders.title: Finance Controller
stakeholders.stance_summary: Requires staged payment tied to proof acceptance and first factory rollout readiness. "I am not approving the full expansion as one upfront commitment." Demands capped enablement scope and insists services cannot become an open-ended line item. Wants proof scorecard and financial transparency: "Do not hide the yellow items. Finance can approve a staged rollout with known conditions." Prefers milestone payment to reference acceptance of closeout pack rather than vague satisfaction. Reconfirmed staged payment tied to acceptance of closeout pack with capped enablement as of 2026-05-04.

stakeholders.name: Henrik Vale
stakeholders.title: Security Architect
stakeholders.stance_summary: Interested in policy templates and data protection reporting. Accepted segmentation model but requested additional evidence on data protection controls. Emphasizes that security policy degradation requires escalation even when backup path is healthy. Wants policy drift report included in proof pack and insists templates do not drift plant by plant: "I need evidence that templates do not drift plant by plant." Advocates for policy template owner naming in alerts to avoid orphaned tickets. Recommends recurring policy drift review as part of close plan. Cautions against overloading plant proof while maintaining security rigor.
